2608.26051.title: The Value of Human Expertise
2608.26051.paper_summary: We consider optimization applications with unknown parameters where the decision maker believes that the optimal value of the nominal problem-the optimization problem they would have solved if the true parameters were known-is unlikely to be large. This belief derives from information that humans have that is not captured in datasets, obtained from domain knowledge and interacting with the physical world. We propose an approach to evaluating policies that provides tighter performance guarantees if the decision maker's belief happens to be correct. Our main result shows that if computing a policy's worst-case performance is a convex program, then the value of human expertise-the maximum improvement in performance guarantees that can be obtained from the belief about the nominal problem-is equal to the minimax gap of a max-min problem. We illustrate our developments in assortment optimization and shortest path problems.
2608.26051.paper_summary_zh: 我們考慮具有未知參數的優化應用，其中決策者認為名義問題的最佳值——如果已知真實參數，他們將解決的優化問題——不太可能很大。這種信念源於人類擁有的信息，這些信息在數據集中未被捕捉，來自於領域知識和與物理世界的互動。我們提出了一種評估政策的方法，如果決策者的信念恰好是正確的，則提供更緊湊的性能保證。我們的主要結果顯示，如果計算政策的最壞情況性能是一個凸規劃，那麼人類專業知識的價值——從對名義問題的信念中可以獲得的性能保證的最大改進——等於一個最大-最小問題的最小最大差距。我們在產品組合優化和最短路徑問題中說明了我們的發展。
